title: DNS over QUIC RFC 9250 0-RTT Replay Protection Verification
verification_method: Focused unit tests for opcode classification, client-side 0-RTT gating, server-side signaled 0-RTT refusal behavior, and existing test regression checks.
scope: This verification covers DNS opcode classification, client-side 0-RTT gating, client-side session-resumption privacy policy checks, and server-side non-replayable 0-RTT refusal when DoqServerOptions.ZeroRttStreamDetector supplies an early-data signal. Transport-native inbound 0-RTT detection remains limited by the transport API as documented in ARC-QUIC-RFC9250-0013.
expected_result: All DoQ tests pass, core SpecTrace validation accepts the RFC 9250 artifacts including slice 0013, and no whitespace hygiene issues are introduced.
status_summary: The DoQ adapter classifies DNS opcodes for replayability, gates 0-RTT on the client side, proves client-side session-resumption and 0-RTT privacy policy, and refuses signaled non-replayable server-side 0-RTT with REFUSED+EDE Too Early before handler dispatch. Transport-native inbound 0-RTT detection is still supplied through the detector seam rather than inferred by the DoQ adapter.
